manifest.title: Coupled Frame-Entrenchment Failure Glossary Graph
manifest.description: Token-efficient positioning graph for the terminology used to diagnose, distinguish, and correct coupled frame-entrenchment failure.

relation_vocabulary.definition: links a glossary root to a term necessary for reconstruction
marks a condition that defeats or weakens diagnosis
links a failure mechanism to a corrective operation

nodes.label: Coupled frame-entrenchment failure
nodes.definition: An emergent failure mode of human-LLM inquiry in which an inadequate human problem representation and frame-conditioned model assistance recursively increase the authority, elaboration, and persistence of that representation, suppressing better-purpose-fit alternatives.
nodes.canonical_use: Use when the coupled interaction, not either participant alone, recursively stabilizes the limiting frame.

nodes.label: Active frame
nodes.definition: The currently operative, purpose-relative organization of objects, relations, operations, constraints, evaluation criteria, and candidate alternatives through which an inquiry is conducted.
nodes.canonical_use: Use for the representation presently governing relevance and action.

nodes.label: Ontological deficit
nodes.definition: An absence, incompleteness, conflation, false separation, misleveling, misbounding, or other distortion in the active frame that limits what can appear as a relevant entity, relation, operation, cause, or intervention.
nodes.canonical_use: Use diagnostically and provisionally; it need not imply one uniquely correct ontology.

nodes.label: Better-purpose-fit representation
nodes.definition: An alternative representation that serves the declared inquiry purpose more adequately while preserving required invariants and surviving tests against evidence, constraints, consequences, and rival frames.
nodes.canonical_use: Prefer this over “correct ontology” when several legitimate projections or scales may coexist.

nodes.label: Corrective structure
nodes.definition: A concept, distinction, relation, operation, causal level, unit of analysis, or rival frame capable of reorganizing the problem and its apparent action space.
nodes.canonical_use: Use for candidate resources that may enable representational repair.

nodes.label: Frame capture
nodes.definition: Conditioning of model assistance on the user-supplied representation such that the representation is treated as the operative world of the task rather than as a revisable hypothesis.
nodes.canonical_use: Use for model-side frame dependence; do not equate with deliberate agreement.

nodes.label: Premise deference
nodes.definition: Preferential treatment of detailed, effort-laden, or confidently stated premises as settled constraints.
nodes.canonical_use: Use when authority is inferred from presentation or investment rather than independent warrant.

nodes.label: Local answer optimization
nodes.definition: Selection of an immediately responsive continuation within the active frame without auditing the larger problem representation.
nodes.canonical_use: Use when a locally useful answer displaces representation-level diagnosis.

nodes.label: Compensatory structure
nodes.definition: A workaround, branch, procedure, artifact, or coordination burden created because the active frame cannot directly represent or perform the required transformation.
nodes.canonical_use: Use without presuming the compensation is avoidable until tested.

nodes.label: Compensatory structure reification
nodes.definition: Conversion of a contingent workaround into an apparent requirement or intrinsic feature of the task.
nodes.canonical_use: Use when the solution path is mistaken for the problem structure.

nodes.label: Effort-derived constraint credibility
nodes.definition: The increase in apparent authority granted to a frame or constraint because substantial labor has already occurred within it.
nodes.canonical_use: Distinguish from sunk-cost persistence: this is an epistemic credibility effect.

nodes.label: Frame-internal success
nodes.definition: A coherent, procedural, symptomatic, metric, social, or institutional success that is compatible with the active frame but does not uniquely validate it.
nodes.canonical_use: Always type the success and ask whether it discriminates among rival frames.

nodes.label: Intervention-induced pseudo-confirmation
nodes.definition: Apparent validation produced when a frame-consistent intervention changes an outcome through several possible mechanisms, while the change is attributed uniquely to the presumed mechanism.
nodes.canonical_use: Use when the intervention is non-diagnostic.

nodes.label: Performative entrenchment
nodes.definition: Reinforcement in which actions generated under a frame alter the external system so that later observations increasingly resemble or support the frame.
nodes.canonical_use: Use when the interaction helps create its own confirming evidence.

nodes.label: Search-neighbourhood contraction
nodes.definition: Progressive narrowing of generated alternatives toward those expressible inside the active frame.
nodes.canonical_use: Use for declining practical accessibility of rival representations.

nodes.label: Frame audit
nodes.definition: A deliberate examination that recovers the objective and invariants, classifies constraint provenance, identifies compensatory structures, and generates rival representations before further optimization.
nodes.canonical_use: Use as the primary corrective procedure.

nodes.label: Ontological escape
nodes.definition: A controlled transition from the active frame to a tested, better-purpose-fit representation.
nodes.canonical_use: Do not use for novelty alone or for discarding real constraints.

nodes.label: Corrective externalization
nodes.definition: Expression of candidate corrective structure in an inspectable, testable, purpose-relative form.
nodes.canonical_use: Use for model output that enables comparison rather than asserting hidden certainty.

nodes.label: Anchoring bias
nodes.definition: Disproportionate influence of an initial value or representation on later judgment.
nodes.canonical_use: Use for the initial influence; CFEF additionally requires coupling and recursive reinforcement.

nodes.label: Confirmation bias
nodes.definition: Preferential search for or interpretation of evidence supporting an existing belief.
nodes.canonical_use: Use for biased evidence handling; CFEF also includes model-generated elaboration and artifacts.

nodes.label: Sycophancy
nodes.definition: Model agreement or accommodation that displaces warranted correction.
nodes.canonical_use: Use only when agreement-seeking is evidenced; frame capture can occur without a salient contradiction.

nodes.label: Automation bias
nodes.definition: Over-reliance on machine-generated recommendations.
nodes.canonical_use: Use for one-way machine authority; CFEF is recursively co-produced.

nodes.label: Einstellung effect
nodes.definition: A familiar solution strategy blocks recognition of a simpler or more adequate one.
nodes.canonical_use: Use for strategy fixation; CFEF adds human-model coupling and reinforcement.

nodes.label: Double-loop learning
nodes.definition: Learning that questions governing assumptions rather than only correcting actions within them.
nodes.canonical_use: Use as a close corrective analogue; it does not itself name the coupled failure.

nodes.label: Genuine irreducible complexity
nodes.definition: Complexity that persists after independent reformulation because required constraints remain operative.
nodes.canonical_use: Do not diagnose CFEF merely because a task is difficult.

nodes.label: Model knowledge absence
nodes.definition: A condition in which the model lacks and cannot plausibly reconstruct the required corrective structure from available evidence.
nodes.canonical_use: Distinguish from failure to externalize reconstructible alternatives.

nodes.label: Deliberate constraint acceptance
nodes.definition: Intentional selection of an expensive or limited path because it serves learning, reproducibility, artistic, political, or other declared purposes.
nodes.canonical_use: Do not optimize away an objective the user intentionally selected.

nodes.label: Temporary scaffolding
nodes.definition: A knowingly simplified and revisable representation used to support bounded action.
nodes.canonical_use: Incompleteness alone is not entrenchment.

nodes.label: Correct frame with poor execution
nodes.definition: Failure caused by implementation defects despite an adequate representation of the problem.
nodes.canonical_use: Treat as execution failure unless recursive representational reinforcement is also present.

nodes.label: Over-reframing
nodes.definition: Unwarranted replacement of an operative frame through novelty, elegance, or speculation while dropping evidence or real constraints.
nodes.canonical_use: Guard against frame vandalism, false hidden causes, and repeated reopening of settled premises.

nodes.label: Scale sufficiency test
nodes.definition: A check whether perfect optimization or elimination of the framed cause could account for the magnitude of the observed outcome.
nodes.canonical_use: Use to falsify structurally insufficient frames.

nodes.label: Invariant ledger
nodes.definition: A declaration of what an alternative preserves, loses, assumes, requires verification of, and introduces.
nodes.canonical_use: Require before adopting a simpler representation.

nodes.label: Constraint provenance
nodes.definition: The source and warrant of a constraint, such as logical, physical, empirical, technical, permission-based, legal, safety, organizational, conventional, inherited, or assumed.
nodes.canonical_use: Classify rather than silently treating all stated limits as equivalent.
